newsitem.title: USA: US says thrift industry has made solid recovery.
newsitem.headline: US says thrift industry has made solid recovery.

text.p: For the first time in the 1990s, not a single U.S. thrift institution is in serious financial trouble, the Office of Thrift Supervision reported Wednesday.
"This achievement is a testament to the solid financial recovery of the thrift industry," OTS director Nicolas Retsinas said in a statement.
"Even though other seriously troubled institutions may be identified in the future, the fact there was none at the end of 1996 is a milestone for the industry," he added.

In mid-1993, at the peak of the industry's troubles, the office listed 65 thrifts as "seriously troubled." Recently, the number has ranged from two to four, down from six in June of last year, OTS said.
At the end of November, two thrifts were in serious trouble. One was subsequently acquired and the other submitted an acceptable recapitalization plan, OTS said.
OTS said 32 institutions remain on its less serious "other troubled" thrift list, the same number as in June of last year.
Retsinas urged Congress to move ahead on thrift charter reform.

"Given the soundness of the industry's financial condition, now is a good time for Congress to begin focusing on modernization of the financial services industry, including bank and thrift charter reform," he said.
Two bills have already been introduced in the House of Representatives that would merge bank and thrift charters.
